column1: # p14 DPM {auto,high} interleaved benchmark, 2026-08-22, AFTER restoring amd_iommu=off.
# This is the confirming A/B for dpm-results.tsv, which was taken earlier the same day on the
# same boot config EXCEPT that the IOMMU was on. Same board, same DIMMs, same server
# (llama-test.service), same harness (bench-dpm.sh, 4 interleaved rounds), same power state.
# The ONLY difference is amd_iommu=off on the kernel command line.
# amd_iommu=off had been removed on 2026-08-21 at 13:13 to unblock the NPU (XDNA2 needs SVA,
# SVA needs the IOMMU -- see npu-after-reboot.sh). Restored 2026-08-22, rebooted 13:15.
# Verified before this run: amd_iommu=off in /proc/cmdline, 0 IOMMU groups, GTT still 49152 MiB.
# RESULT -- steady state, round 1 dropped, n=3:
#   arm    metric   IOMMU on   IOMMU off    gain     P16s    vs P16s
# CONCLUSION: the IOMMU was the whole thing. +19-26% prefill and +15-16% generation from one
# boot parameter. The replacement mainboard is now within 3% of the P16s on both arms -- i.e.
# EXONERATED. The earlier conclusion that this board was "23% slower at the top end" was a
# confound: it compared a P16s measured with amd_iommu=off against a p14 measured with the
# IOMMU on. Retracted.
# Two details that confirm the mechanism rather than just the effect:
#  1. Power tracks throughput. At dpm-high the GPU now draws 53.1 W where it drew 46.7 W with
#     the IOMMU on, at the SAME 2900 MHz -- the "low power" was the GPU stalling on address
#     translation, not a power cap being imposed. It now matches the P16s' 54.8 W.
#  2. At dpm-auto the IOMMU-off run is FASTER at a LOWER clock (1922 vs 2169 MHz, +19.4% PP).
#     With the IOMMU on the GPU was clocking higher to compensate and still losing.
